title: Credential escrow and forensic procedure
body:
Purpose:

This runbook documents the operational procedures and audit expectations for credential escrow retrieval, forensic inspection, and automated evidence export to our SIEM. It complements existing secret lifecycle notes by focusing on the contingency / emergency access path (escrow), how RBAC v2 decisions appear in audit logs, and the minimal set of artifacts we must capture and retain for a compliant incident review.

Scope and audience:

- Audience: SecOps, on-call SREs, Platform security engineers, and designated approvers (security leadership).
- Applies to: All production secrets stored in Redwood-managed secret stores (primary vault cluster, KMS-encrypted file escrow on object storage, and hardware-backed key escrow).
- Out of scope: Developer local secrets, ephemeral developer API tokens that are not registered in the credential inventory.

Definitions / quick glossary:

- Escrow: Read-only snapshot copy of a secret and its metadata stored in a secured object store for emergency retrieval.
- Break-glass: The sanctioned emergency approval flow to grant temporary access to an escrowed credential.
- RBAC v2: Our second-generation role/permission model (roles are scoped, attribute-based policies).
- Evidence bundle: A timebound set of artifacts (audit logs, SIEM events, access approvals, hash of retrieved secret, retrieval command logs).

Preconditions (what must exist before retrieval):

1) Credential must be registered in the canonical inventory (see inventory_id field on secret metadata). Unregistered secrets are escalated to SRE+SecEng for triage.
2) Escrow snapshot exists and is time-stamped (escrow:yyyy-mm-ddThh:mmZ).
3) At least two approvers from the authorized approver group (security_leads or on_call_secops) are available OR an emergency exec override (documented separately).

High-level flow (summary):

1) Incident owner creates an emergency-access ticket (JIRA SEC-xxxx) and posts a retrieval request in #sec-ops with the inventory_id and justification.
2) Two approvers approve in Jira and confirm in Slack thread. Approvals MUST include a reason and a retention period for the secret copy.
3) SecOps runs the Escrow Retrieval command (internal vault-escrow CLI) which performs the following atomically: logs retrieval attempt to audit stream, fetches escrowed object, computes SHA256 hash, writes the hash and retrieval metadata to the evidence bucket, and emits a structured audit event.
4) Retrievee receives credential via ephemeral workstation session (no emailing of secrets). All access is recorded and the session is timeboxed to the approved retention period.

Detailed step-by-step runbook (operational):

1) Create emergency ticket:
   - Template title: [ESCROW-RTRV] inventory_id=<ID> – short impact sentence
   - Required fields: inventory_id, env (prod/stage), justification, approvers (suggested), maximum retention (hours), CI/CD jobs affected.
   - Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-1284 (example)

2) Notify approvers (Slack + Jira):
   - Post in #sec-ops with the ticket link. Tag approvers @sec-leads.
   - Approvers must click "approve" in the Jira workflow and paste the approval text in the Slack thread.

3) Validate RBAC v2 authorization:
   - Confirm that both approvers have the RBAC attributes required for this secret class (sensitivity: high/medium/low). Use the RBAC v2 lookup tool: /tools/rbacv2-check --principal <approver> --resource <inventory_id>.
   - Record the returned policy snapshot (policy_version: v2.x) in ticket.

4) Run the escrow retrieval (SecOps only):
   - Command (example): vault-escrow retrieve --id <inventory_id> --ticket SEC-1284 --requester <operator> --dest /tmp/escrow-rtrv-<id>.json
   - Automated side-effects: the CLI emits a JSON audit record to the audit pipeline containing: event_type:escrow_retrieve, actor, inventory_id, ticket, request_hash, timestamp, rbac_snapshot_id, hash_of_secret.
   - CLI will perform a pre-fetch dry-run to ensure KMS unwrap is permitted for the retrieval principal. If dry-run fails, abort and escalate.

5) Immediate evidence captures (atomic and mandatory):
   - Append the retrieval JSON event to the audit topic (audit.events.produced).
   - Copy full HTTP/CLI session transcript for the retrieval host to the evidence bucket.
   - Persist SHA256(secret) and the path of the escrow object; do NOT store plaintext secret in long-term evidence.
   - Trigger an automated SIEM export for a correlated incident_alert (see SIEM mapping below).

Break-glass / emergency override path:

- If approvers cannot be reached and service impact > P0 threshold, on-call SecEng can trigger the emergency override. This requires:
  - A post-facto review by SecOps within 24 hours.
  - Supervisor-level logging and an exec notification.
  - The emergency override will record event_type:escrow_override with override_code and approver_unavailable flag.

RBAC v2 interactions and audit expectations:

- RBAC v2 policy decisions are always recorded as part of the escrow_retrieve event. Required audit keys: rbac_policy_id, decision (allow/deny), decision_reason, policy_snapshot_url, evaluated_attributes (list).
- When a retrieval is allowed because of a temporary policy grant (e.g., approval grant), the evidence bundle must include the grant token and its TTL.
- For denials, the CLI returns a structured denial event that includes suggested next steps (request approval or escalate).

Audit log schema (minimal required fields for escrow-related events):

- event_id (uuid)
- event_type (escrow_retrieve | escrow_override | escrow_create | escrow_delete)
- inventory_id
- actor_principal (email/SSO id)
- actor_role_snapshot (comma list)
- rbac_policy_id
- decision (allow|deny)
- request_ticket (jira key)
- timestamp_utc
- object_path (obscured except for hash)
- secret_hash_sha256
- evidence_bucket_path
- approvers (list)
- retention_ttl_seconds
- correlation_id (incident id)
- retrieval_host

All audit events must be emitted as newline-delimited JSON to our audit topic and forwarded to the SIEM with the mapping below.

SIEM export mapping (Elastic / Splunk friendly):

- siem.event.category = "credential_escrow"
- siem.event.action = event_type
- siem.actor.id = actor_principal
- siem.actor.role = actor_role_snapshot
- siem.policy.id = rbac_policy_id
- siem.policy.decision = decision
- siem.file.hash.sha256 = secret_hash_sha256
- siem.file.path = evidence_bucket_path
- siem.alert.severity = mapping(decision, impact, secret_sensitivity)
- siem.related.ticket = request_ticket
- siem.time = timestamp_utc

Sample SIEM document (conceptual):

{
  "@timestamp": "2025-02-28T15:12:03Z",
  "event": { "category": "credential_escrow", "action": "escrow_retrieve" },
  "actor": { "id": "n.patel@redwood.ai", "role": "on_call_secops,sec_admin" },
  "policy": { "id": "rbacv2-2025-02-a", "decision": "allow" },
  "file": { "hash": { "sha256": "<hash>" }, "path": "s3://evidence-bucket/escrow/escrow-rtrv-<id>.json" },
  "related": { "ticket": "SEC-1284" }
}

Evidence automation notes (what the pipeline should do):

- On escrow_retrieve event: trigger a serverless job that copies: evidence transcript, rbac snapshot, ticket snapshot (Jira export) into a write-once path and computes aggregated hashes.
- Generate a signed manifest.json that references all artifacts and includes a manifest_signature computed with HSM key id=escrow-manifest-signer.
- Notify stakeholders via secure channel (SecOps-only email + Slack private thread) with link to manifest.

Post-retrieval cleanup and rotation verification:

1) If retrieval occurred to replace a broken secret, confirm rotation pipeline ran: run ./scripts/verify-rotation --inventory-id <id> which will: check all consumers via service discovery, check last-successful-deploy timestamps, and validate the new secret hash matches stored rotated hash.
2) If rotation failed, rollback plan: re-revoke any temporary credentials, restore original config, and open a followup dev/sre ticket.

Retention and legal hold:

- Evidence bundles for P0 incidents: retain 7 years (legal review may extend).
- Routine retrievals: retain 90 days by default unless escalated.
- Any legal hold MUST be applied by legal@redwood.ai and recorded in the manifest.

Security hygiene and hard requirements:

- Never send plaintext secret via email or chat. Ephemeral workstation sessions or secure vault-proxy must be used.
- Secret hashes are stored long-term; plaintext must be destroyed after rotation and only kept transiently in the ephemeral session.
- All CLI tools must be run from approved bastion hosts with SCIM SSO enforcement.

Quick checklist for on-call (copyable):

- [ ] Create SEC ticket with inventory_id and justification
- [ ] Tag approvers and collect two approvals
- [ ] Run rbacv2-check and paste snapshot into ticket
- [ ] Run vault-escrow retrieve (record CLI output)
- [ ] Ensure audit event emitted and SIEM alert triggered
- [ ] Save evidence manifest and hash only
- [ ] Verify rotation pipeline if replacing secret

Open questions / TODOs:

- How should we handle multi-party escrow (secrets that require threshold decryption)? Add additional steps.
- Confirm retention durations with Privacy/Legal for EU customer secrets (GDPR constraints).
- Add automations to include commit SHAs for any code that consumed the retrieved secret.

References and useful links:

- RBAC v2 design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design
- Credential inventory index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Credential+Inventory
- Jira template: https://jira.redwood.ai/secure/CreateIssue.jspa?pid=SEC
- Slack: #sec-ops (pinned: "escrow-retrieval-template")

Notes to reviewers:

- This is intended as the canonical emergency retrieval runbook. Please check the RBAC v2 attribute names and the audit schema field names for compatibility with the audit producer code (audit-producer v1.9).
- I left several TODOs inline — please add any additional compliance constraints you think belong here.

Document history:

- 2024-10-12: initial draft by N. Patel
- 2024-11-03: added SIEM mapping and RBAC v2 keys (M. Lee)
- 2025-02-28: incorporated evidence automation manifest spec (E. Gomez)

Unstructured notes / scribbles:

- If approvers are on PTO, should we fall back to a standing "rotating approver" list? Maybe automated escalation to on-call manager.
- Consider short-lived KMS-derived decryption keys for escrow retrieval rather than unwrapping the master key each time.

End of document.
